[USER] User expressed concern about measures to prevent or punish corruption within political systems and their effectiveness.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Anti-corruption laws and regulations criminalize corruption, including bribery, embezzlement, and nepotism, with penalties such as fines and imprisonment.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Independent anti-corruption agencies, like the ICPC in Nigeria and the CVC in India, investigate and prosecute corruption cases.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Codes of conduct and ethics govern the behavior of politicians and public officials, prohibiting corrupt practices and conflicts of interest.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Whistleblower protection laws encourage reporting of corruption without fear of retaliation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Transparency measures, such as open budgeting and public procurement disclosure, increase accountability within political systems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The effectiveness of anti-corruption measures varies by context and implementation level; some countries effectively combat corruption while others do not.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Enforcement of anti-corruption measures varies across countries; some enforce them strongly while others do not.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The effectiveness of anti-corruption measures depends on political will, institutional capacity, and public support.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Continuous monitoring and evaluation of anti-corruption measures are crucial for effectiveness.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Citizens, civil society organizations, and the media play essential roles in holding governments accountable for enforcing anti-corruption measures.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Raising public awareness and mobilizing citizens can empower them to hold public officials accountable.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Encouraging whistle-blowing through protection measures can help report corrupt practices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Promoting international cooperation can support anti-corruption efforts.
